candidates.claim: sw-ot-01 defines a read-write SNMP community that is not restricted by any ACL, while the management policy requires read-only communities restricted to MGMT hosts.
candidates.remediation: Remove the read-write community on sw-ot-01, or change it to read-only restricted by an ACL that permits only 10.10.99.50.

candidates.claim: EDGE_IN permits any Internet source to tcp/443 on the fw-01 outside address 203.0.113.2, and the ASA HTTP server is enabled, although device management is permitted only from MGMT on the mgmt interface.
candidates.remediation: Remove or narrow the EDGE_IN entry for tcp/443 to 203.0.113.2 so that firewall HTTPS/ASDM is reachable only from MGMT on the mgmt interface.

candidates.claim: The current sw-ot-01 configuration adds an snmp-server community line that is absent from the approved baseline and must be reconciled.
candidates.remediation: Reconcile the added snmp-server community on sw-ot-01 with the approved baseline by removing it or documenting approval.

clarifications.question: The registry says only OT-facing ports may be active in VLAN 10, but it also approves trunks carrying VLAN 10 on sw-ot-01 Gi1/0/24 {10,99}, sw-core-01 Gi1/0/22 {10,99} and sw-core-01 Gi1/0/24 {10,20,30,99}. Should approved trunk carriage of VLAN 10 be treated as compliant with I3, or do these uplink trunks count as active VLAN 10 ports that violate the rule?
